key_insight: Tuning the flame-spraying O2/C2H2 ratio directly improved Ni–Cr–B–Si coating densification, adhesion, and surface finish, with an optimum hardness at the intermediate ratio.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical process-control knob for producing more durable self-fluxing coatings on corrosion-resistant steel components.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings onto AISI 321 stainless steel using a Metal Coat 6PM-II system.
Varied the O2/C2H2 ratio to 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 while monitoring spray conditions with Accuraspray 4.0.
Measured microstructure, porosity, microhardness, surface roughness, and adhesion strength.
evidence_signal: Raising O2/C2H2 reduced porosity from 1.97 ± 0.13% to 0.90 ± 0.09%, lowered roughness from 4.70 ± 0.09 μm to 2.99 ± 0.11 μm, and increased adhesion from 22.14 ± 4.3 MPa to 35.02 ± 3.9 MPa, while peak hardness reached 1051.7 HV at 1.1.
watch_item: The abstract reports strong property trends, but the optimal setting may depend on substrate, powder feed, torch setup, and service environment, so direct transfer to other systems should be validated.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
